title: More Americans Are Becoming Entrepreneurs—And They’re Starting Solo in the AI Era
excerpt: More Americans are starting new businesses, but today’s entrepreneurs aren’t hiring the way they used to.
content_html:
Kara Greenberg

Thu, July 23, 2026 at 11:22 AM CDT 2 min read

Key Takeaways

  • New business applications are up from a year ago, but those planning to hire are down, according to a report this week from Bank of America Institute.

  • The spread of AI tools has made it easier for founders to start with leaner operations, researchers at the bank said.

More Americans are starting new businesses, but today's entrepreneurs aren't hiring the way they used to.

While a growing number of Americans are starting new businesses, with applications up some 15% year-over-year as of June, those with plans to hire workers are on the decline, according to a report from Bank of America Institute this week. 

That's contributed to a widening divergence between the number of new businesses and those hiring workers in recent years, as "more companies are being started with leaner operating models," the report said. That could be thanks in part to the rise of AI, which has made it easier for entrepreneurs to launch businesses with fewer workers, according to the the bank's researchers.

"If AI or other digital tools can help founders automate administrative tasks, bookkeeping or content creation, the upfront need for employees could be lower than in past startup cycles," Bank of America Institute wrote. "That would help explain why headline applications can rise even as those with planned wages lag."

Why This Is Significant

While AI could make it easier for Americans to start new business with fewer employees, it could also mean fewer new jobs created for today's job seekers—at least initially.

AI-enabled founders of one-person businesses, or "solopreneurs," are increasingly driving American's new business boom, a Nasdaq analysis of Census Bureau data published last month found. In fact, "the acceleration in business formation has come almost entirely from those one-person companies," said Nasdaq economist Michael Normyle, citing data showing applications by one-person companies have surged 20% since early 2025, while those from companies likely to hire remained nearly flat.

These shifts in new businesses' hiring trends could have broader implications for the economy, though it remains to be seen whether these business might hire more employees later. A Bank of America analysis of small business operations last month found that while many small businesses are boosting their spending on the technology, there are "still limited signs that AI is replacing jobs" in the longer term.

"For now, we think evidence suggests that AI may be making it easier to form a business rather than a proven driver of broad-based small business productivity gains," Bank of America Institute wrote in Tuesday's report.

content_html_zh:
卡拉·格林伯格

2026 年 7 月 23 日星期四上午 11:22 CDT 阅读时间 2 分钟

要点

  • 美国银行研究所本周发布的一份报告显示，新申请的企业数量较一年前有所增加，但计划招聘的数量有所下降。
  • 该银行的研究人员表示，人工智能工具的普及使创始人更容易开始精简运营。

越来越多的美国人开始创办新企业，但今天的企业家不再像以前那样招聘员工。

美国银行研究所本周发布的一份报告显示，虽然越来越多的美国人开始开办新企业，截至 6 月份申请数量同比增长约 15%，但计划雇用员工的美国人却在减少。

报告称，这导致近年来新企业数量与雇用员工的企业数量之间的差距不断扩大，因为“越来越多的公司开始采用更精简的运营模式”。 该银行的研究人员表示，这可能部分归功于人工智能的兴起，它使企业家更容易以更少的工人创办企业。

美国银行研究所写道：“如果人工智能或其他数字工具可以帮助创始人自动化管理任务、簿记或内容创建，那么对员工的前期需求可能会低于过去的初创周期。” “这将有助于解释为什么尽管计划工资的申请滞后，但总体申请量仍会上升。”

为什么这很重要

虽然人工智能可以让美国人更容易地以更少的员工开展新业务，但这也可能意味着为当今的求职者创造的新就业机会减少——至少在最初是这样。

纳斯达克对上个月发布的人口普查局数据进行的一项分析发现，人工智能的个人企业创始人或“个体企业家”正在日益推动美国的新商业繁荣。 纳斯达克经济学家 Michael Normyle 表示，事实上，“企业组建的加速几乎完全来自于那些一人公司”。他援引的数据显示，自 2025 年初以来，一人公司的申请数量激增了 20%，而来自可能招聘的公司的申请数量几乎持平。

新企业招聘趋势的这些变化可能会对经济产生更广泛的影响，尽管这些企业以后是否会雇佣更多员工还有待观察。 美国银行上个月对小企业运营的分析发现，虽然许多小企业正在增加在技术上的支出，但从长远来看，“人工智能正在取代工作岗位的迹象仍然有限”。

美国银行研究所在周二的报告中写道：“目前，我们认为有证据表明人工智能可能使企业组建变得更容易，而不是广泛的小企业生产率提高的经过验证的驱动因素。”
